entities.name: Sima Tan
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sima Tan, an eminent Chinese astrologer, astronomer, and historian, laid the foundational groundwork for the monumental *Shiji* (Records of the Grand Historian) during the Western Han dynasty. Born in an unknown year and dying in 109 BCE, Sima Tan served as the Grand Historian (Taishi Ling) at the imperial court, a position that combined the roles of astronomer, calendar-maker, and archivist. His ambition was to compile a comprehensive history of the Chinese world from its mythical origins to his own time, aiming to synthesize the disparate historical records and philosophical traditions that preceded him. This grand project was conceived as a moral and political guide for future generations, reflecting the intellectual ferment and imperial consolidation of the early Han.

As Grand Historian, Sima Tan was responsible for observing celestial phenomena, interpreting omens, and maintaining the imperial archives. His intellectual curiosity, however, extended far beyond these administrative duties. He was deeply versed in the Six Schools of Thought (Yin-Yang, Confucianism, Mohism, Legalism, School of Names, Taoism), and his own philosophical leanings, particularly towards Huang-Lao Taoism, influenced the syncretic approach evident in the *Shiji*'s design. He meticulously gathered historical materials, organized them into annals, tables, treatises, hereditary houses, and memoirs, establishing a narrative framework that would become the standard for subsequent Chinese historiography. Though he initiated this monumental task, a significant portion of the writing and compilation remained unfinished at the time of his death.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sima Tan's visionary initiation of the *Records of the Grand Historian* established the foundational framework for Chinese historiography that endured for over two millennia, directly influencing all subsequent dynastic histories. His work, completed by his son Sima Qian, became the prototype for understanding and recording China's past.
